name: Bancha Ongkosit
current_role: Founder and Chairman, KCE Electronics PCL (Thailand)
profile: Former advertising executive who founded KCE Electronics (originally Kuang Charoen Electronics, named after his father) in 1982; it is now Southeast Asia's largest printed-circuit-board maker and a top global PCB supplier to the auto industry. The firm rebuilt after the 1997 crisis; his Cornell-educated son Pitharn has been CEO since 2013.
interesting_fact: KCE is described as the largest PCB manufacturer in Southeast Asia and among the top five global PCB suppliers for the automotive industry; Bancha became a billionaire in 2021 as auto-electronics demand surged.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in advertising and launched KCE in 1982 with just 12 million baht of capital.
notes: Low public profile; son Pitharn Ongkosit (CEO) is the public face of KCE. Best route is company IR. Chairman title per MarketScreener listing; deep-cut figures from Forbes 2021 coverage (forbes.it page blocked to direct fetch, verify before use).

name: Hyuntae Kim
current_role: CEO (Corporate Management), Voronoi Inc. (Kosdaq: 310210), Incheon, South Korea
profile: Former securities-industry asset-management chief (eBest, Hanwha, KB Securities) who invested in and took over Voronoi, the precision-oncology biotech his younger brother Hyun-seok founded in 2015; he became CEO in 2016 and listed it on Kosdaq in 2022. Its AI-assisted platform produced cancer candidates VRN10 (HER2) and VRN11 (EGFR), both in Phase 1 since 2025.
interesting_fact: Voronoi's stock rose about 190% in 2025 on its AI-driven cancer pipeline, making Kim, who holds roughly 35%, one of South Korea's newest billionaires despite the company having minimal revenue.
deep_cut_fact: A finance man with no biotech background, he bet on his brother's startup in 2016 by buying 100,000 newly issued shares at 10,000 won each while Voronoi was still private; he holds business and MBA degrees from Seoul National University.
notes: Co-leads with R&D CEO Kim Dae-kwon; Hyuntae handles business side. Voronoi has a US subsidiary (Voronoi USA, President Jaeyoung Ahn) which may be an easier English-language route. IR@voronoi.io is the best published channel.

name: Thomas Patterson
current_role: General Partner/managing member, Madrone Capital Partners (Denver); Director, StubHub Holdings (NYSE: STUB) since Sept 2025
profile: Thomas A. Patterson, 60, has been a general partner at Madrone Capital Partners since 2005, investing in founder/family-owned businesses, emerging-market middle-class plays and technology; earlier he was at Weston Presidio (1995-2004) and McKinsey. He joined StubHub's board at its September 2025 IPO and also sits on Castleton Commodities and Teya boards.
interesting_fact: His StubHub '10% owner' status comes from Madrone funds holding ~21.7% of StubHub (75.8M shares); Madrone's managing members are Patterson, Jameson McJunkin and Walmart chairman Gregory Penner, and Patterson disclaims beneficial ownership of those shares.
deep_cut_fact: A Harvard history graduate (AB, plus HBS MBA), he is active in environmental conservation and chairs the Stanford Natural Capital Alliance Advisory Council. He also sat on StoneCo's board 2018-2022, a Brazilian fintech, and on Castleton Commodities, an energy trader, which is relevant to an energy podcast.
notes: The ~$913M SEC-derived net worth is almost certainly Madrone fund holdings (Walton/Penner-linked vehicle), not his personal wealth, since he disclaims beneficial ownership. Madrone keeps a low profile and has no public contact found; StubHub IR is the only published route.

name: Mai Haoyun
profile: Listed by Hurun China 2026 jointly with Mai Gang as Pop Mart shareholders. Mai Gang (Michael Mai) was Pop Mart's 2012 angel investor (about RMB 2 million) and a pre-IPO shareholder; no public information was found on Mai Haoyun (麦浩云) specifically, who is presumably a relative or co-holder.

name: Li Hong
current_role: Co-founder and major shareholder, Guangzhou ZWSOFT Co. (中望软件, SSE STAR: 688083); exact current title not confirmed
profile: Li Hong (李红) is a co-founding shareholder of ZWSOFT, the Guangzhou maker of ZWCAD (2D, DWG-compatible) and ZW3D CAD software, listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2021. Records show her holding 19.5% alongside chairman/GM Du Yulin (68.5%) in 2010, and she was one of three promoters when the firm became a joint-stock company in Nov 2006.
interesting_fact: ZWSOFT is one of China's leading domestic industrial-design software makers, positioned as a home-grown alternative to Autodesk/Dassault CAD tools amid China's push for software self-sufficiency.
notes: Very common name; no public biography found. Hurun lists her with Du Yulin (chairman/GM), who is the public face. Personal relationship to Du not verified here. Route via ZWSOFT board secretary/IR (ir@zwsoft.com).

name: Zhou Guangyu
current_role: General Manager and Director, Beijing BDStar Navigation Co. (北斗星通, SZSE: 002151), appointed GM July 2026
profile: Zhou Guangyu (周光宇) is a director of BDStar Navigation, a leading Chinese maker of BeiDou/GNSS satellite-navigation chips, modules and positioning products, and the son of founder-chairman Zhou Ruxin, with whom he is an acting-in-concert controlling shareholder (about 51.4M shares). In July 2026 he succeeded his father as general manager.
interesting_fact: BDStar, founded by his father Zhou Ruxin, is named after China's BeiDou ('Big Dipper') satellite navigation system and is one of the core commercial players building chips and receivers for it.
notes: Low public profile; no personal biography (education/age) found in accessible sources. Father Zhou Ruxin (chairman) is the better-known figure. Board secretary is Pan Guoping (潘国平); route via company. Satellite navigation/PNT is tangentially relevant to energy/data-center infrastructure (timing).

name: Liu Yuanbing
current_role: Chairman and President, Mayland Group (美林基业集团), Guangzhou (per company-profile listing; currency not verified)
profile: Liu Yuanbing (刘远炳) founded Guangzhou-based Mayland Group in 1999; it develops residential property (Meilin Xinhaoting, CSA/Nanhang Garden, Meilin Coast Garden, Meilin Lakeside Garden) and also operates in construction, trade, hotels and property management. He has served as a vice president of the Guangzhou Real Estate Industry Association. He last appeared on the Hurun China list in 2022.
interesting_fact: Mayland was ranked among Guangzhou's 20 most competitive property developers and named a 'China Excellent Enterprise' in 2003.
notes: Very private; little public biography. No working official website found (mayland.cn is a parked domain). Dropped off Hurun after 2022; given the Chinese property downturn, verify current status of the group before outreach. Web-search budget ran out during this profile, so research was limited.

name: Li Qiang
current_role: Listed by Hurun China (2015-2026) as the owner behind Pechoin (百雀羚), Shanghai; exact title not verified
profile: Hurun attributes this fortune to Pechoin (百雀羚), China's oldest domestic skincare brand (founded 1931 in Shanghai). The brand was privatised in 2000 as Shanghai Pehchaolin Daily Chemical Co. and rebuilt into one of China's largest cosmetics brands; no public biography of Li Qiang (李强) as its owner could be found.
interesting_fact: Pechoin's tin of cold cream was favoured by the Soong sisters in the 1930s, and in 2013 Peng Liyuan presented Pechoin products as a state gift in Tanzania, sparking a 'guochao' domestic-brand craze.
notes: Extremely common name and very private owner; his role at Pechoin could not be confirmed from accessible sources (web-search budget exhausted mid-lane, Baidu Baike blocked). Pechoin's published general contact (bql1931@pechoin.com) is the only route found.

name: Chuo Yung-Tsai
current_role: Founder and Group President, HIWIN Technologies (上銀科技, TWSE: 2049), Taichung, Taiwan; also founder of HIWIN Mikrosystem
profile: Chuo Yung-Tsai (卓永財, b. 1942), a Hakka from a tenant-farming family in Zhubei, Hsinchu, was a Bank of Communications executive who turned around Taiwan's largest nut maker in 1983, then bought ball-screw maker Ho Feng Precision and in 1989 founded HIWIN, now the world's second-largest ball-screw maker with motion-control and robotics units worldwide. His son Eric Chuo is chairman.
interesting_fact: HIWIN bought German ball-screw maker Holzer in 1993, just four years after founding, giving the Taiwanese company an early European manufacturing base; it is now the world's No. 2 ball-screw maker.
deep_cut_fact: He once posted on Yahoo! Kimo Knowledge+ under the alias '猛男一號' ('Macho Man No. 1'), chatting about the machinery industry and encouraging female students to study mechanical engineering. He also funded a library at Liujia Elementary School in memory of his elder brother.
notes: Accounting graduate of Tamkang University with a management master's from University of San Francisco; author of a book on foreign-exchange practice. Honorary chairman of Taiwan's machine tool & accessory builders' association. Best route is HIWIN corporate/IR.

name: Pang Qingnian
current_role: Chairman, China Youngman Automobile Group / Jinhua Neoplan Vehicle Co. (status uncertain; group in distress since ~2014)
profile: Pang Qingnian (庞青年, b. 1958, Tiantai, Zhejiang) went from tyres to vehicles, founding Jinhua Youngman Automobile in 1996 and, via a 2000 partnership with Germany's Neoplan, building luxury coaches; he later made Youngman Lotus cars with Proton/Lotus technology. The car unit was declared bankrupt in 2017.
interesting_fact: Through the Neoplan joint venture, Youngman at one point held close to 70% of China's market for luxury coaches priced above RMB 800,000.
deep_cut_fact: He began in 1979 with a small adhesive-tape workshop in his hometown, then in 1986 started a chemical plant in Pan'an making tyres for handcarts, bicycles and motorcycles, the path that led him into building cars.
notes: CAUTION: per Chinese Wikipedia, Youngman Lotus went bankrupt (2017), Pang was placed under a police fraud investigation in 2017 and has been on China's dishonest-debtor list 20+ times. Last on Hurun in 2013; the wealth figure is stale. Not recommended for outreach; no public contact found.

name: Sha Xiaolan
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Funshine Culture Group (锋尚文化, SZSE ChiNext: 300860), Beijing
profile: Sha Xiaolan (沙晓岚, b. 1962, Nanjing) is a stage-lighting designer trained at the Shanghai Theatre Academy who worked for the PLA General Political Department Song and Dance Troupe and the China Oriental Performing Arts Group before founding Funshine. The firm designs and produces mega-events, live shows and cultural-tourism projects; it listed on ChiNext in 2020.
interesting_fact: He was chief director and chief producer of the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Games opening ceremony, and lighting chief designer for the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics opening ceremony.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming a listed-company boss he was a working lighting designer, and he gave People's Daily an exclusive interview on how the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics opening-ceremony lighting was designed. He was also chief producer of the Hangzhou show 'Most Memorable is Hangzhou' (最忆是杭州).
notes: Member of the Jiusan Society. Company email is from the exchange-disclosed company profile (Eastmoney F10); board secretary is Li Yong (李勇). Hurun co-lists Wang Fangyun. Large-scale light shows have a strong energy/tech angle.
